answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Each submission hangs on the inlet of a task receipt, and the orchard is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, voided if the audit panel is not diverse, no identity may audit its own recruit. What survives to the kernel is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short.
